He—may Allah have mercy on him—was asked:

A man leased the land of an orchard from Mashārif al-Ajnās for a specified period, then died, leaving children. The rent was payable in instalments of twenty dirhams each year. The deceased tenant’s children have been asked to pay the entire rent immediately. Can they be required to pay the full rent, or should it be collected from them in its annual instalments?

He replied:

In these circumstances, his children are not required to pay the entire rent immediately. However, if the owners of the land do not trust them to discharge this obligation, they may require them to provide someone who will guarantee payment of the rent as its instalments fall due.

 بِمَنْزِلَةِ أَنْ تَنْتَقِلَ الْمَنْفَعَةُ إلَى مُشْتَرٍ أَوْ مُتَّهِبٍ مِثْلَ أَنْ يَبِيعَ الْأَرْضَ أَوْ يَهَبَهَا أَوْ يُورَثَ فَإِنَّ الْأَرْضَ مِنْ حِينِ الِانْتِقَالِ تَلْزَمُ الْمُشْتَرِيَ وَالْمُتَّهِبَ وَالْوَلَدَ:
 فِي أَصَحِّ قَوْلَيْ الْعُلَمَاءِ كَمَا عَلَيْهِ عَمَلُ الْمُسْلِمِينَ؛ فَإِنَّهُمْ يُطَالِبُونَ الْمُشْتَرِيَ وَالْوَارِثَ بِالْحِكْرِ قِسْطًا لَا يُطَالِبُونَ الْحِكْرَ جَمِيعَهُ مِنْ الْبَائِعِ. أَوْ تَرِكَةِ الْمَيِّتِ؛ وَذَلِكَ لِأَنَّ الْمَنَافِعَ لَا تَسْتَقِرُّ الْأُجْرَةُ إلَّا بِاسْتِيفَائِهَا فَلَوْ تَلِفَتْ الْمَنَافِعُ قَبْلَ الِاسْتِيفَاءِ سَقَطَتْ الْأُجْرَةُ بِالِاتِّفَاقِ. وَلِهَذَا كَانَ مَذْهَبُ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ وَغَيْرِهِ أَنَّ الْأُجْرَةَ لَا تُمْلَكُ بِالْعَقْدِ؛
 بَلْ بِالِاسْتِيفَاءِ وَلَا تُمْلَكُ الْمُطَالَبَةُ إلَّا شَيْئًا فَشَيْئًا وَلِهَذَا قَالَ:
 إنَّ الْإِجَارَةَ تَنْفَسِخُ بِالْمَوْتِ.
 وَالشَّافِعِيِّ وَأَحْمَد وَإِنْ قَالَا:
 تُمْلَكُ بِالْعَقْدِ وَتُمْلَكُ الْمُطَالَبَةُ إذَا سَلَّمَ الْعَيْنَ فَلَا نِزَاعَ أَنَّهَا لَا تَجِبُ إلَّا بِاسْتِيفَاءِ الْمَنْفَعَةِ وَلَا نِزَاعَ فِي سُقُوطِهَا بِتَلَفِ الْمَنَافِعِ قَبْلَ الِاسْتِيفَاءِ. وَلَا نِزَاعَ أَنَّهَا إذَا كَانَتْ مُؤَجَّلَةً لَمْ تُطْلَبْ إلَّا عِنْدَ مَحَلِّ الْأَجَلِ. فَإِذَا خَلَّفَ الْوَارِثُ ضَامِنًا وَتَعَجَّلَ الْأَجَلَ الَّذِي لَمْ يَجِبْ إلَّا مُؤَخَّرًا مَعَ تَأْخِيرِ اسْتِيفَاءِ حَقِّهِ مِنْ الْمَنْفَعَةِ كَانَ هَذَا ظُلْمًا لَهُ مُخَالِفًا لِلْعَدْلِ الَّذِي هُوَ
translated_text:
sounder of the scholars’ two views. For the heir who inherits the right to use the property must pay the rent for the use he enjoys. Thus, if the deceased owed debts, the heir could not reserve that use for himself while treating the rent as a claim competing with those of the creditors, on the grounds that it is a debt owed by the deceased, like the purchase price owed under an effective sale.

This is comparable to the right of use passing to a purchaser or the recipient of a gift, as when someone sells the land, gives it away, or leaves it to be inherited. From the time of transfer, responsibility for the land falls upon the purchaser, the recipient of the gift, or the child, according to the sounder of the scholars’ two views. This is also the established practice among Muslims: they require the purchaser and the heir to pay the land rent in instalments, rather than demanding the entire rent from the seller or the deceased’s estate.

This is because entitlement to rent is not finally established until the corresponding use has been enjoyed. If that use becomes unavailable before it is enjoyed, the rent ceases to be due, by agreement. Hence, the position of Abū Hanīfah and others is that ownership of the rent is acquired not through the contract, but as the use is enjoyed, and the right to demand payment arises only progressively. For this reason, he held that the lease terminates upon death.

Although al-Shāfiʿī and Ahmad held that ownership of the rent is acquired through the contract, and that the right to demand it arises when the property itself is handed over, there is no dispute that liability for it arises only upon enjoyment of the use. Nor is there any dispute that it ceases to be due if the use becomes unavailable before it is enjoyed. Likewise, there is no dispute that, when payment is deferred, it cannot be demanded until the agreed due date.

Thus, if the heir provides a guarantor, yet payment that was not due until a later date is brought forward while his enjoyment of the use to which he is entitled remains deferred, this is an injustice to him, contrary to the justice that is

If the heir does not agree to become liable for the rent, and the lessor says, “I will not make the use available to you so that you may enjoy his entitlement to it,” then requiring the heir to pay the rent immediately from the estate, while enjoyment of the use remains deferred, plainly entails injustice to him.

If the leased property is an endowment or the like, its administrator has no right to collect all the rent in advance. Even stipulating this would not make it permissible. For if he does not own the future benefits and is entitled to their rent only as they arise in the future, collecting it in advance without any need for repairs amounts to taking something to which the endowment’s beneficiary is not yet entitled.

He also answered:

Payment of the rent in advance is not required according to the sounder of the scholars’ two views, especially if the rented property is an endowment. Collecting rent in advance for an endowment is permissible only for repairs and similar needs, because successive generations of beneficiaries are entitled to its benefits. Each group is entitled to the rent for the benefits arising during its own time. If they receive payment in advance for future use, they will have taken compensation for something in the endowment to which they are not entitled, and this is impermissible.

However, if those entitled to the property ask the tenant’s heirs to provide a guarantor for the rent, they have that right. The sum remains a liability of the heirs, backed by a knowledgeable guarantor for the endowment’s beneficiaries in respect of its occupant. Moreover, even if the property were not an endowment, the debt would not fall due upon the debtor’s death. He was asked:

A man rented an orchard for ten years and received the rental sum. He then died after five years of the term had elapsed, leaving five years remaining on the lease. He had heirs, who were evicted a year after his death. Is the owner permitted to terminate the orphans’ lease, or not?

He answered:

According to the vast majority of scholars, the lessor has no right to terminate the lease merely because the tenant has died. Some, however, hold that the rent owed by the tenant becomes immediately due upon his death and is collected from his estate; if he leaves no estate, the lessor may terminate the lease.

Others hold that the rent does not become immediately due if the heirs secure its payment with collateral or a guarantor. Rather, they must pay it to him as the deceased used to do. This is the more evident of the two views. And Allah knows best.

He was asked—may Allah have mercy on him:

Some people live in a village near the mountain in the Fayyūm region, where half is seen in some years. This year, a three-year lease of the local land was drawn up for the village elders before the previous lease had expired and before the crops had been cleared from the land. Is this lease valid?

He answered:

If they were wrongfully compelled to enter into the lease, it is neither valid nor binding, without any disagreement among the imams. If, however, they leased it voluntarily or were rightfully compelled to do so, while the land was still leased to others, this is called a lease commencing at a future date. This has been the practice of Muslims in most times and places, for, as with a contract of sale, there is nothing in it that would invalidate the lease. It makes no difference whether enjoyment of the benefit begins at the time of the contract or not.

The fact that the tenant does not take possession immediately after concluding the contract does not invalidate it. Taking possession follows what the contract requires and entails. If it requires possession immediately afterward, possession must be taken immediately afterward; if it requires possession to be deferred, possession must be taken when the contract requires it, since what is taken into possession

(١)
 كَمَا هُوَ مَذْهَبُ مَالِكٍ وَأَحْمَد. وَلِهَذَا لَوْ أُقْبِضَ الْعَيْنَ الْمُؤَجَّرَةَ كَانَتْ فِي الْمَنْفَعَةِ مَعَ خَرَاجِ تَصَرُّفِ الْمُسْتَأْجِرِ فِيهَا بَاقِيَةٌ عَلَى ضَمَانِ الْمُؤَجِّرِ فَلَوْ تَلِفَتْ بِآفَةِ سَمَاوِيَّةٍ كَانَتْ مِنْ ضَمَانِهِ بِاتِّفَاقِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ. وَكَذَلِكَ يَقُولُ مَالِكٍ وَأَحْمَد وَغَيْرُهُمَا فِي بَيْعِ الثِّمَارِ إذَا أَصَابَتْهَا جَائِحَةٌ. وَبِالْجُمْلَةِ فَلَا يَحْرِمُ مِنْ الْعُقُودِ إلَّا مَا حَرَّمَهُ نَصٌّ أَوْ إجْمَاعٌ أَوْ قِيَاسٌ فِي مَعْنَى مَا دَلَّ عَلَى النَّصِّ أَوْ الْإِجْمَاعِ فَكُلُّ ذَلِكَ مُنْتَفٍ فِي الْإِجَارَةِ الْمُضَافَةِ وَإِذَا اسْتَأْجَرَ الْأَرْضَ وَفِيهَا زَرْعٌ لِلْغَيْرِ فَإِنَّهُ يَبْقَى لِصَاحِبِهِ بِأُجْرَةِ الْمِثْلِ كَمَا تَبْقَى لَوْ لَمْ يُؤَجِّرْ الْأَرْضَ. وَاَللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ.

translated_text:
under the contract is not something the Lawgiver has required to be delivered in a particular manner; rather, this is governed by what the two parties have stipulated in the contract. Accordingly, if someone sells date palms that have not been pollinated, their fruit belongs to the seller according to Mālik, al-Shāfi'ī and Imam Ahmad, as indicated by the Sunnah. The seller may enter the property to attend to his fruit, even though this is inconsistent with complete possession.

Likewise, if someone sells a married slave woman, the right to marital relations remains with her husband and is not included in what the purchaser takes possession of for himself, by agreement of the four imams. The same applies to leased property according to most scholars. For this reason, groups of these scholars consider it valid to continue enjoying an asset’s benefits in cases of sale, gift, endowment, manumission and the like, as indicated by the hadith … (1). This is the position of Mālik and Ahmad.

Thus, when possession of leased property is handed over, it remains the lessor’s responsibility with respect to its benefit, even while it yields income through the tenant’s use. If it is destroyed by a natural calamity, the lessor bears the loss, by agreement of the Muslims. Mālik, Ahmad and others hold the same view concerning the sale of fruit when a calamity strikes it.

In short, no contract is forbidden except one prohibited by a scriptural text, scholarly consensus, or an analogy corresponding in meaning to what a text or consensus establishes. None of these grounds exists in a lease commencing at a future date. If someone leases land containing crops belonging to another person, those crops remain there for their owner at the prevailing rent, just as they would remain had the land not been leased. Allah knows best.

وَسُئِلَ:
عَنْ رَجُلٍ اسْتَأْجَرَ حَانُوتًا وَقَدْ جَاءَ إنْسَانٌ زَادَ عَلَيْهِ فِي الْحَوَانِيتِ فَقَدَّمَهُ. فَهَلْ تُفْسَخُ إجَارَةُ الْمُسْتَأْجِرِ الْحَانُوتَ الْوَاحِدَ؟ أَمْ لَا؟ .
فَأَجَابَ:
الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ،
 إذَا اسْتَأْجَرَهَا مِنْ الْمَالِكِ أَوْ وَكِيلِهِ أَوْ وَلِيِّهِ لَمْ يَكُنْ لِأَحَدِ أَنْ يَقْبَلَ عَلَيْهِ زِيَادَةً وَلَا يُخْرِجَهُ قَبْلَ انْقِضَاءِ مُدَّتِهِ وَإِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ بَيْنَهُمَا كِتَابٌ وَلَا شُهُودٌ بَلْ مَنْ قَالَ:
 اذْهَبْ اُكْتُبْ عَلَيْك إجَارَةً فَأَشْهَدَ عَلَيْهِ الْمُسْتَأْجِرُ بِالْإِجَارَةِ وَمَكَّنَهُ الْمُؤَجِّرُ مِنْ السُّكْنَى فَهَذِهِ إجَارَةٌ لَازِمَةٌ. وَاَللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ.
وَسُئِلَ:
عَنْ رَجُلٍ زَادَ عَلَى قَوْمٍ فِي بَيْتٍ لِيَسْكُنَ فِيهِ. فَهَلْ يَأْثَمُ بِذَلِكَ؟ وَهَلْ يَجِبُ تَعْزِيرُهُ عَلَى ذَلِكَ؟ .
فَأَجَابَ:
قَدْ ثَبَتَ فِي الصَّحِيحَيْنِ عَنْ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ أَنَّهُ قَالَ:
 
{لَا يَحِلُّ لِمُسْلِمِ أَنْ يَسُومَ عَلَى سَوْمِ أَخِيهِ وَلَا يَخْطُبَ عَلَى خِطْبَةِ أَخِيهِ}
 فَإِذَا
translated_text:
He was asked:

A man rented a shop, then someone else came and offered a higher rent for the shops and was given preference over him. May the lease of the tenant who rented the single shop be terminated, or not?

He replied:

Praise be to Allah.

If he rented the premises from the owner, his agent or his guardian, no one may accept a higher offer over his or evict him before his lease expires, even if there is no written agreement or witnesses. Indeed, if the lessor says, “Go and have a lease drawn up in your name,” and the tenant has the lessor’s agreement to the lease witnessed, and the lessor allows him to occupy the premises, this constitutes a binding lease. Allah knows best.

He was asked:

A man offered a higher rent than some people for a house so that he could live in it. Does he incur sin by doing so? Must he be subjected to discretionary punishment for this?

He replied:

It is established in the two Sahīh collections that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“It is not lawful for a Muslim to make a competing offer against his brother’s offer, or to propose marriage over his brother’s proposal.”

Thus, if

فَأَجَابَ:
إذَا كَانَ الْأَمْرُ عَلَى مَا ذُكِرَ فَمِثْلُ هَذَا عَيْبٌ فِي الْعَقَارِ وَإِذَا لَمْ يَعْلَمْ بِهِ الْمُسْتَأْجِرُ حَالَ الْعَقْدِ فَلَهُ أَنْ يَفْسَخَ الْإِجَارَةَ وَلَا أُجْرَةَ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ حِينِ الْفَسْخِ. وَاَللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ.
translated_text:
the landlord had already settled on letting the premises to someone, no one else may offer a higher rent. How much more so when that person is already living there and continuing to occupy the premises! Whoever does this deserves discretionary punishment. Allah knows best.

He was asked:

A man rented a house next to a bad neighbour. The tenant went to the landlord and said, “I am not willing to have him as my neighbour. Either move him elsewhere or return my rent.”

The landlord replied, “I will move him today.” The tenant then swore an oath invoking triple divorce that if the neighbour did not move that day, he would not live in the house. The tenant did not move out of the house. He then requested the rent, but it was not given to him.

He replied:

If the matter is as described, something like this constitutes a defect in the property. If the tenant was unaware of it when the contract was concluded, he is entitled to terminate the lease, and no rent is due from him from the time of termination. Allah knows best.

translated_text:
He—may Allah have mercy on him—was asked:

A man owns a property whose fair rent is five dirhams. He gives the tenants money to help them financially, and they pay a higher rent. Is this permissible or not?

He replied:

If he lends someone ten dirhams on condition that he rent his shop from him for more than the fair rent, this is impermissible by Muslim consensus. Indeed, even if this were arranged between them without a stipulation, it would be invalid and forbidden according to most scholars.

(As authentically reported from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, he said:

“It is not lawful to combine a loan with a sale, to impose two conditions in a sale, to make a profit from something for which one has not assumed liability, or to sell what one does not have.”

Al-Tirmidhī said: “This is an authentic hadith.”) (*)

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, thus forbade selling to someone while also lending to him, because the borrower would favour the lender in the sale on account of the loan. How much more objectionable, then, if he stipulates, along with the loan, that the borrower rent from him and favour him, when he has nothing! If the debtor is in hardship, he must be given time until he is able to pay.

Allah Most High says:

“O you who believe, fear Allah and give up what remains of interest, if you are believers.”

“If you do not, then be warned of war from Allah and His Messenger. But if you repent, you may retain your principal, neither wronging nor being wronged.”

“If the debtor is in hardship, then grant him time until he is able to pay; and for you to
translated_footnote:

It appears that the word “hadith” was omitted before “sahīh” (authentic), so that the phrase should read, “as established in the authentic hadith.” The customary expression “as established in al-Sahīh” refers to reports found in either of the two Sahīh collections, those of al-Bukhārī and Muslim, whereas this hadith appears in neither. After quoting the hadith, the Shaykh—may Allah have mercy on him—mentioned that al-Tirmidhī recorded it. He was asked:

A soldier has an allotment, and someone compelled him to lease it to him. He leased it under duress for two hundred dirhams, then showed that it was worth four thousand dirhams. Is this lease valid or not?

He replied:

Praise be to Allah. If he compelled him to enter into the lease without right, it is invalid. If he deceived him, the soldier has the right to rescind the lease. And Allah knows best.

He was asked:

A man collected money for someone at a rate of six dirhams per thousand, whereas the customary rate is twelve dirhams. He incurred expenses in collecting it and was misled by the stipulated terms. What is his position?

He replied:

If the hirer deceived and misled the person he hired into accepting less than the customary rate, with a disparity greater than people ordinarily accept, the latter has the right to demand the customary remuneration.

He was asked:

A man leased a property to another man for a fixed term. Towards the end of that term, someone else offered a higher rent, so he leased it to him. The first tenant objected, saying, “This property is under lease to me.” Is he entitled to object?

He replied:

If he leased it for the period following the first tenant’s lease, the first tenant has no right to object. And Allah knows best.

He—may Allah have mercy on him—was asked:

A man owns shops occupied by people who have no lease from the owner. Others have now offered several times more for the shops than the current occupants. May the owner lease the shops to them and accept the higher rent?

The Answer

He replied:

If they are unjust usurpers who have occupied the premises without the owner’s permission, evicting such people does not require an offer of higher rent. Rather, they must leave even before any higher rent is offered, and the owner may evict them before such an offer. Nor

translated_text:
is it lawful for the owner to demand a stipulated rent from them; they owe only the fair rental value.

If the lessor is the trustee of an endowment or the guardian of an orphan, allowing them to remain when he could evict them constitutes injustice and transgression on his part. This impugns his integrity and his authority to act in that capacity.

If, however, they occupy the premises according to the customary practice of tenants—for example, someone approaches the owner and says, “Lease me such-and-such premises for such-and-such an amount,” and the owner replies, “Go and have your agreement witnessed”—then the tenant, but not the lessor, has witnesses attest to his undertaking, and the premises are handed over to him. When the occupant wishes to leave, the owner does not allow him to do so. This constitutes a valid lease under Islamic law.

Whoever says, “This is not a valid lease under Islamic law; the occupant may not leave without the owner’s permission, yet the owner may evict him whenever he wishes,” has contradicted the consensus of the Muslims. If the lease is valid under Islamic law, it is binding on both parties; if it is invalid, it is invalid for both parties. Whoever makes it binding on the tenant but terminable at will by the lessor has contradicted the consensus of the Muslims.

If the lessor is the trustee of an endowment or an orphan’s property, hands the premises over to the occupant, instructs him to have a lease drawn up recording his obligations, and demands both the lease document and the stipulated rent, yet says, “I have not granted him a valid lease under Islamic law,” this impugns his integrity and his authority to act in that capacity. For the jurists hold two views concerning a valid lease under Islamic law:

translated_text:
The first is that a lease or hiring contract is concluded through whatever people customarily regard as such. Thus, if someone hands his food to a cook who cooks for payment, or his clothes to a washer who washes for payment, or entrusts work to a weaver, tailor, or similar craftsman who customarily works for payment, they are entitled to fair remuneration. Likewise, if someone enters a bathhouse, boards a boat, or rides an animal, as is customary with mounts and conveyances made available for hire, the provider is entitled to the fair customary charge.

How much more so, then, if someone says, “Lease it to me for such-and-such an amount,” and the other replies, “Go and draw up a lease,” whereupon he draws it up and the premises are handed over to him? According to these jurists, this is a valid lease under Islamic law. This is the view of most jurists, including Mālik, Abū Hanīfah, Imam Ahmad, and others.

The second view is that a particular form is indispensable, just as a similar requirement has been stipulated for sales. This is the position of those among al-Shāfiʿī’s followers who hold this view. Anyone who believes this must not impose a rental obligation except in this manner. If someone believes that rent can be validly stipulated only in this manner, yet leases the premises in the customary way, hands them over, and demands the stipulated rent, then, when an increase is in question, claims that no lease exists, his claim is not to be accepted. This is injustice: if he adheres to a legal school, he must adhere to it both when it serves his interests and when it works against them.

As for holding the lease to be valid when it serves his interests, but invalid when it works against them, this is neither acceptable nor permissible, by the consensus of the Muslims. Whoever persists in such conduct is unjust by the agreement of the Muslims. Indeed, he is a sinful person, disqualified from giving testimony or exercising such authority.

translated_text:
He—may Allah have mercy on him—was asked:

A man was renting a nearby plot of land. While he was away travelling, someone bought the house adjoining the land he was renting, built it up, and incorporated it into his own house. What must be done?

He replied:

(*) He has no right to seize the rented land along with other property or incorporate it into his house. By doing so, he is an unjust usurper. The tenant may either terminate the lease on this account, in which case his obligation to pay rent lapses, or continue the lease and demand payment from the usurper for his use of the land.

He may also choose whether to leave the building on the land or have it taken down, if this falls within the terms of his lease. If it does not fall within those terms, he may not act with respect to the land without the owner’s permission. And Allah knows best.

original_text:
وَسُئِلَ:
عَنْ رَجُلٍ وَكَّلَ رَجُلًا عَلَى أَنَّهُ يَسْتَأْجِرُ لَهُ وَيُؤَجِّرُ عَنْهُ وَيَبِيعُ عَنْهُ وَيَبْتَاعُ لَهُ. فَاسْتَأْجَرَ لِمُوَكِّلِهِ حِصَّةً بِقَرْيَةِ مُدَّةً مَعْلُومَةً إجَارَةً صَحِيحَةً لَازِمَةً فقايله مُدَّةَ الْإِيجَارِ مِنْ غَيْرِ أَنْ يَكُونَ الْمُوَكِّلُ وَكَّلَهُ فِي الْمُقَايَلَةِ. فَهَلْ هَذِهِ الْمُقَايَلَةُ صَحِيحَةٌ؟ وَهَلْ الْإِيجَارُ بَاقٍ عَلَى أَصْلِهِ الصَّحِيحِ يَسْتَحِقُّهُ لِلْمُوَكِّلِ؟ وَيَسْتَحِقُّ الْمُؤَجِّرُ الْإِجَارَةَ وَالْحَالُ هَذِهِ؟
فَأَجَابَ:
الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، إذَا تَعَذَّرَ اسْتِيفَاءُ الْمُسْتَأْجِرِ الْأُجْرَةَ الَّتِي يَسْتَحِقُّهَا فَلَهُ فَسْخُ الْإِجَارَةِ كَمَا إذَا تَعَذَّرَ اسْتِيفَاءُ الْمُشْتَرِي الثَّمَنَ إذَا طَلَبَ الْفَسْخَ وَالْحَالُ هَذِهِ وَإِجَارَةُ الْمُسْتَأْجِرِ لِلْوَكِيلِ قَدْ كَانَ فَعَلَ مَا وَجَبَ عَلَيْهِ وَلَيْسَ هَذَا مِنْ الْمُقَايَلَةِ الْجَائِزَةِ الَّتِي تَفْتَقِرُ إلَى إذْنِ الْمُوَكِّلِ. وَاَللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ.
translated_text:
He was asked:

A man appointed another as his agent to rent property for him, let property on his behalf, sell on his behalf, and purchase for him. The agent rented a share in a village for his principal for a specified term under a valid, binding lease. He then agreed to cancel the lease during its term, although the principal had not authorized him to agree to its cancellation. Is this cancellation by mutual agreement valid? Does the lease remain valid as originally concluded, with its benefits belonging to the principal? Is the lessor entitled to the rent in these circumstances?

He replied:

Praise be to Allah. If the tenant cannot collect the rent to which he is entitled, he may cancel the lease, just as when a purchaser cannot recover the price, if he requests cancellation in these circumstances. As for the tenant’s leasing to the agent, he had done what was required of him. This is not one of those permissible cancellations by mutual agreement that require the principal’s permission. And Allah knows best.

original_text:
وَسُئِلَ:
عَنْ جَمَاعَةٍ بِيَدِهِمْ إقْطَاعٌ وَفِي الْإِقْطَاعِ أَرْضٌ عَاطِلَةٌ وَأَذِنُوا لِشَخْصِ أَنْ يُؤَجِّرَهَا؛ فَأَجَّرَهَا مُدَّةَ ثَلَاثِينَ سَنَةً وَلَمْ يُشَاوِرْ الْوَكِيلُ الْمُقْطَعِينَ عَلَى الثَّلَاثِينَ سَنَةٍ فَهَلْ تَجُوزُ هَذِهِ الْإِجَارَةُ؟ أَمْ لَا؟
فَأَجَابَ:
لَا تَصِحُّ هَذِهِ الْإِجَارَةُ إلَّا إذَا كَانَتْ بِإِذْنِ الْمُقْطَعِينَ أَوْ مَا يَقْتَضِي الْإِذْنَ فِيهَا. فَأَمَّا مُجَرَّدُ الْإِذْنِ فِي الْإِجَارَةِ مُطْلَقًا الَّذِي يَقْتَضِي فِي الْعُرْفِ سَنَةً أَوْ سَنَتَيْنِ أَوْ نَحْوَ ذَلِكَ فَلَا يُفْهَمُ مِنْهُ الْإِذْنُ فِي هَذِهِ الْمُدَّةِ الطَّوِيلَةِ فَلَا تَصِحُّ الْإِجَارَةُ بِمُجَرَّدِهِ.
وَسُئِلَ:
عَنْ رَجُلٍ بِيَدِهِ إقْطَاعٌ يَشْهَدُ بِهِ مَنْشُورُهُ وَأَنَّهُ ضَمِنَ بَعْضَ نَوَاحِي الْإِقْطَاعِ لِمَنْ يَزْرَعُهَا وَيَنْتَفِعُ بِهَا مُدَّةً مُعَيَّنَةً ثُمَّ انْتَقَلَ الْإِقْطَاعُ الَّذِي بِيَدِهِ إلَى غَيْرِهِ. فَهَلْ يَصِحُّ الْإِيجَارُ الْأَوَّلُ؟ وَهَلْ إذَا صَحَّ يَصِحُّ الْإِيجَارُ عَلَى الْمُقْطَعِ الثَّانِي أَوْ يُفْسَخُ؟ وَهَلْ لِلْمُقْطَعِ أَنْ يَمْنَعَ الْمُؤَجِّرِينَ الِانْتِفَاعَ؟
translated_text:
He was asked:

A group holds a land grant containing unused land. They authorized someone to let it, and he leased it for thirty years without consulting the grant-holders about this thirty-year term. Is this lease valid or not?

He replied:

This lease is valid only if the grant-holders authorized it, expressly or implicitly. Mere general permission to let the land—which customarily means a lease of one or two years, or thereabouts—cannot be understood as permission to lease it for such a lengthy term. The lease is therefore not valid on the basis of that permission alone.

He was asked:

A man holds a land grant, as attested by his official grant document. He leased certain parts of it to someone to cultivate and benefit from for a specified term. The grant he held was then transferred to someone else. Is the original lease valid? If it is valid, is it binding upon the second grant-holder, or is it to be terminated? May the grant-holder prevent those leasing the land from benefiting from it?

original_text:
فَأَجَابَ:
 الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ. نَعَمْ يَصِحُّ الْإِيجَارُ الْأَوَّلُ؛ لَكِنْ إنْ شَاءَ الْمُقْطَعُ الثَّانِي أَمْضَاهُ؛ بَلْ مِنْ حِينِ أُقْطِعَهَا صَارَتْ لَهُ فَإِنْ شَاءَ أَجَّرَهَا لِذَلِكَ الْمُسْتَأْجِرِ وَإِنْ شَاءَ لَمْ يُؤَجِّرْهُ. فَإِنْ كَانَ لِلْمُسْتَأْجِرِ فِيهَا زَرْعٌ أَبْقَاهُ بِأُجْرَةِ الْمِثْلِ إلَى حِينِ كَمَالِهِ وَإِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ فِيهَا لَا عَيْنٌ وَلَا مَنْفَعَةٌ فَلَا شَيْءَ لَهُ.
وَسُئِلَ - رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ -:
عَنْ رَجُلٍ لَهُ إقْطَاعٌ فَحَضَرَ إلَيْهِ شَخْصٌ وَطَلَبَ إيجَارَ الطِّينِ مِنْهُ فَأَجَّرَهُ طِينَهُ لِلشَّخْصِ الْمَذْكُورِ مِنْ غَيْرِ أَنْ يَكْشِفَ طِينَهُ وَسَأَلَ عَنْهُ وَكَانَ الْمُسْتَأْجِرُ ذَكَرَ لِلْآخَرِ إنْ لَمْ تُؤَجِّرْ طِينَك وَإِلَّا يَبُورُ فَخَشِيَ الْجُنْدِيُّ مِنْ بَوَرَانِ الطِّينِ فَأَجَّرَهُ مِنْ غَيْرِ أَنْ يَكْشِفَ ثُمَّ حَضَرَ شَخْصٌ آخَرُ مِنْ أَهْلِ النَّاحِيَةِ وَعَرَّفَ الْجُنْدِيَّ أَنَّ الْمُسْتَأْجِرَ اسْتَأْجَرَ طِينَك بِدُونِ الْقِيمَةِ فَإِنَّ الشَّرِكَةَ طِينُهُمْ مُسَجَّلٌ بِأَكْثَرَ مِنْ هَذِهِ الْقِيمَةِ. فَهَلْ يَجُوزُ لِلْجُنْدِيِّ أَنْ يَفْسَخَ الْإِجَارَةَ الْمَكْتَبِيَّةَ؟ وَيُؤَجِّرَ لِغَيْرِهِ بِقِيمَتِهِ سَنَةً؟ أَمْ لَا؟
فَأَجَابَ:
الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ،
 إذَا كَانَ الْمُسْتَأْجِرُ قَدْ دَلَّسَ عَلَى الْمُؤَجِّرِ:
 مِثْلَ أَنْ يَكُونَ قَدْ أَخْبَرَهُ عَنْهُ بِمَا يَنْقُصُ قِيمَتَهُ وَلَمْ يَكُنْ الْأَمْرُ كَذَلِكَ فَلِلْمُؤَجِّرِ فَسْخُ الْإِجَارَةِ.
translated_text:
He replied:

Praise be to Allah. Yes, the original lease is valid. However, the second grant-holder may uphold it if he wishes. Indeed, the land became his from the moment it was granted to him, so he may lease it to that tenant or decline to do so. If the tenant has crops growing on it, he is to allow them to remain at the prevailing rent until they mature. If the tenant has neither tangible property nor any benefit in the land, he is entitled to nothing.

He was asked—may Allah have mercy on him:

A man held a land grant. Someone approached him and asked to lease the agricultural land, and he leased it to that person without inspecting it; he also inquired about it. The tenant had told the other man, “Unless you lease out your land, it will lie fallow.” Fearing that the land would lie fallow, the soldier leased it without inspecting it. Then someone else from the locality came and informed the soldier, “The tenant has leased your land for less than its rental value, for the partners’ land is registered at a higher rent than this.” May the soldier cancel the written lease and lease the land to someone else for a year at its proper rental value, or not?

He replied:

Praise be to Allah. If the tenant deceived the lessor—for example, by giving him information about the land that would diminish its rental value when the facts were otherwise—the lessor may cancel the lease.

original_text:
وَكَذَلِكَ إنْ أَخْبَرَهُ بِأَنَّهُ لَيْسَ هُنَاكَ مَنْ يَسْتَأْجِرُهُ وَكَانَ لَهُ هُنَاكَ طُلَّابٌ وَأَمْثَالُ ذَلِكَ. وَاَللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ.
وَسُئِلَ - رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ -:
عَنْ جُنْدِيٍّ اسْتَأْجَرَ طِينًا مِنْ أَمِيرٍ وَانْتَقَلَ عَنْ الْإِقْطَاعِ وَاخْتَارَ الْمُسْتَأْجِرُ الْفَسْخَ عَنْ الْإِجَارَةِ وَجَاءَ الْأَمِيرُ الْمُسْتَجَدُّ وَطَلَبَ مِنْهُ التَّحْضِيرَ. فَهَلْ يَلْزَمُهُ ذَلِكَ؟
فَأَجَابَ:
إذَا انْتَقَلَ الْإِقْطَاعُ إلَى آخَرَ انْفَسَخَتْ الْإِجَارَةُ مِنْ حِينِ انْتِقَالِهِ؛ فَإِنَّ الْمَنْفَعَةَ الْحَادِثَةَ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ لَمْ تَكُنْ مِلْكًا لِلْأَوَّلِ وَلَا لِلثَّانِي. وَالْمُقْطَعُ إنْ شَاءَ يُؤَجِّرُ وَإِنْ شَاءَ لَا يُؤَجِّرُ وَالْمُسْتَأْجِرُ إنْ شَاءَ اسْتَأْجَرَ مِنْهُ وَإِنْ شَاءَ لَا يَسْتَأْجِرُ مِنْهُ. لَيْسَ لِوَاحِدِ مِنْهُمَا إلْزَامُ الْآخَرِ لَا بِإِجَارَةِ وَلَا لَهُ إلْزَامُهُ بِتَحْضِيرِ.
translated_text:
The same applies if he told him that no one there wished to lease it when there were, in fact, prospective tenants, and in similar cases. Allah knows best.

He was asked—may Allah have mercy on him:

A soldier leased agricultural land from an emir, who subsequently ceased to hold the land grant. The tenant chose to terminate the lease, but the newly appointed emir came and demanded tahdīr from him. Is he obliged to comply?

He replied:

When the land grant passes to another person, the lease terminates from the moment of its transfer, for the right to use the land accruing thereafter had belonged to neither the first nor the second. The grant-holder may lease it out or decline to do so, and the tenant may lease it from him or decline to do so. Neither may compel the other to enter into a lease, nor may either demand tahdīr from the other.

original_text:
وَسُئِلَ:
عَنْ رَجُلٍ اسْتَأْجَرَ أَرْضًا ثُمَّ حَدَثَتْ مَظْلِمَةٌ عَلَى الْبَلَدِ وَطَلَبُوا مِنْهُ أَنْ يَغْرَمَ فِي الْمَظْلِمَةِ. فَهَلْ يَلْزَمُ الْمُسْتَأْجِرَ شَيْءٌ؟ أَمْ لَا؟
فَأَجَابَ:
الْمَظَالِمُ لَا تَلْزَمُ هَذَا وَلَا هَذَا. لَكِنْ إذَا وُضِعَتْ عَلَى الزَّرْعِ أُخِذَتْ مِنْ رَبِّ الزَّرْعِ وَإِنْ وُضِعَتْ عَلَى الْعَقَارِ أُخِذَتْ مِنْ الْعَقَارِ إذَا لَمْ يَشْتَرِطْ عَلَى الْمُسْتَأْجِرِ فَإِذَا كَانَ مَا اشْتَرَطَ لَمْ يَدْخُلْ فِيمَا اشْتَرَطَ عَلَى الْمُسْتَأْجِرِ وَقَدْ وُضِعَ عَلَى الْعَقَارِ دُونَ الزَّرْعِ أُخِذَتْ مِنْ رَبِّ الْأَرْضِ وَإِنْ وُضِعَ عَلَى الزَّرْعِ أُخِذَ مِنْ الْمُسْتَأْجِرِ؛ وَإِنْ وُضِعَ مُطْلَقًا رُجِعَ فِي ذَلِكَ إلَى الْعَادَةِ فِي مِثْلِهِ.
وَسُئِلَ - رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ -:
عَنْ أَمِيرٍ دَخَلَ عَلَى بَلَدٍ وَهِيَ مُسْتَأْجَرَةٌ لِشَيْخِهَا وَبَعْضُ الْأَرْضِ مَشْغُولَةٌ بِزِرَاعَةِ أَقْصَابٍ وَالْأَقْصَابُ مُسْتَمِرَّةٌ فِي عَقْدِ إيجَارِ الْمُسْتَأْجِرِ مِنْ قَبْلِ دُخُولِ الْأَمِيرِ عَلَى الْإِقْطَاعِ وَإِلَى حِينِ انْفِصَالِهِ. فَهَلْ إذَا
translated_text:
He was asked:

A man leased some land, after which an unjust levy was imposed on the locality, and he was asked to contribute towards it. Is the tenant obliged to pay anything or not?

He replied:

Unjust levies are not binding on either party. However, if they are imposed on the crops, they are collected from the owner of the crops; if they are imposed on the property, they are collected from the property, unless the tenant has been made responsible for them by stipulation. Thus, if the stipulated terms did not include such a levy among the tenant’s obligations, and it was imposed on the property rather than the crops, it is collected from the landowner. If it was imposed on the crops, it is collected from the tenant. If it was imposed without specifying either, the customary practice in such cases is followed.

He was asked—may Allah be pleased with him:

An emir took over a locality that was leased to its headman. Some of the land was planted with cane, and the cane remained covered by the tenant’s lease from before the emir assumed possession of the land grant until he relinquished it. So, if

original_text:
كَانَتْ أَرْضُ الْأَقْصَابِ مُسْتَمِرَّةٌ فِي عَقْدِ إيجَارِ الْمُسْتَأْجِرِ قَبْلَ الدُّخُولِ وَإِلَى حِينِ الْخُرُوجِ يَبْطُلُ حُكْمُ الْإِيجَارِ؟ أَوْ يَسْتَمِرُّ حُكْمُهُ؟
فَأَجَابَ:
إيجَارُ الْمُقْطَعِ لِلْأَرْضِ يَصِحُّ وَلَهُ أَنْ يُؤَجِّرَهَا لِمَنْ يَزْدَرِعُهَا قَصَبًا وَغَيْرَ قَصَبٍ. وَكَذَلِكَ لِلْمُسْتَأْجِرِ مِنْهُ أَنْ يُؤَجِّرَهَا لِغَيْرِهِ بِحُكْمِ مَا اسْتَأْجَرَهَا. وَإِذَا مَاتَ ذَلِكَ الْمُقْطَعُ أَوْ أَقْطَعَ إقْطَاعَهُ فَالْمُقْطَعُ الثَّانِي لَا يَلْزَمُهُ إجَارَةُ الْأَوَّلِ وَلَيْسَ لَهُ أَنْ يَقْلَعَ مَا لِلْمُسْتَأْجِرِ فِيهَا مِنْ الزَّرْعِ وَالْقَصَبِ مَجَّانًا؛ بَلْ هُوَ مُخَيَّرٌ إنْ شَاءَ أَنْ يَبْقَى زَرْعُهُ وَقَصَبُهُ بِأُجْرَةِ مُسْتَأْنَفَةٍ بِمِثْلِ الْأُجْرَةِ الْأُولَى أَوْ أَقَلِّ أَوْ أَكْثَرِ كَمَا يَتَرَاضَيَانِ بِهِ؛ لَكِنْ لَيْسَ لَهُ أَنْ يُلْزِمَ الْمُسْتَأْجِرَ بِأَكْثَرِ مِنْ أُجْرَةِ الْمِثْلِ. وَإِذَا اسْتَأْجَرَهَا صَاحِبُ الْقَصَبِ وَالزَّرْعِ صَحَّتْ الْإِجَارَةُ؛ فَإِنَّهُ يَتَمَكَّنُ مِنْ الِانْتِفَاعِ بِهَا؛ وَلَوْ اسْتَأْجَرَهَا غَيْرُهُ جَازَ عَلَى الصَّحِيحِ وَقَامَ غَيْرُهُ فِيهَا مَقَامَ الْمُؤَجِّرِ إنْ شَاءَ أَنْ يَبْقَى زَرْعُهُ وَقَصَبُهُ بِأُجْرَةِ الْمِثْلِ وَإِنْ شَاءَ أَنْ يُؤَجِّرَهُ إيَّاهَا بِرِضَاهُ. وَاَللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ.
translated_text:
the land planted with cane remained covered by the tenant’s lease from before the emir assumed possession until he relinquished it, does the lease cease to have legal effect, or does it remain in force?

He replied:

A lease of the land granted by its land-grant holder is valid, and he may lease it to someone who will cultivate cane or other crops. Likewise, his tenant may sublet it to someone else under the terms of his own lease.

If that land-grant holder dies or his grant is reassigned, the new holder is not bound by the former holder’s lease. However, he may not uproot the tenant’s crops and cane without compensation. Rather, he has the option of allowing the tenant’s crops and cane to remain at a newly agreed rent, whether equal to, lower than, or higher than the original rent, as the two parties mutually agree. He may not, however, compel the tenant to pay more than the fair rental value.

If the owner of the cane and crops leases the land, the lease is valid, since he is able to benefit from it. If someone else leases it, that too is permissible according to the correct view. That person then takes the lessor’s place: he may allow the crops and cane to remain in return for the fair rental value, or he may lease the land to their owner with his consent.

And Allah knows best.

عَمَّنْ لَهُ قِيرَاطٌ فِي بَلَدٍ فَأَجَّرَهُ لِشَخْصِ بِمِائَةِ إرْدَبٍّ وَسِتِّينَ إرْدَبًّا؛ بِنَاقِصِ عَنْ الْغَيْرِ بِثَمَانِينَ إرْدَبًّا وَذَلِكَ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَشْمَلَهُ الرَّيُّ. فَهَلْ تَصِحُّ الْإِجَارَةُ قَبْلَ شُمُولِ الرَّيِّ؟ وَهَلْ لَهُ أَنْ يَطْلُبَ الْقِيمَةَ؟

إذَا كَانَتْ هَذِهِ الْبِلَادُ مِمَّا تُرْوَى غَالِبًا صَحَّتْ إجَارَتُهَا عِنْدَ عَامَّةِ الْفُقَهَاءِ قَبْلَ أَنْ يُرْوَى؛ وَإِنَّمَا النِّزَاعُ فِي مَذْهَبِ الشَّافِعِيِّ. فَظَاهِرُ مَذْهَبِهِ جَوَازُ إجَارَةِ ذَلِكَ. كَمَذْهَبِ سَائِر الْأَئِمَّةِ. وَمَا يُوجَدُ فِي بَعْضِ كُتُبِهِ مِنْ إطْلَاقِ الْعَقْدِ قَدْ فَسَّرَهُ أَئِمَّةُ مَذْهَبِهِ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ. وَمَا زَالَتْ أَرْضُ مِصْرَ تُؤَجَّرُ قَبْلَ شُمُولِ الرَّيِّ فِي أَعْصَارِ السَّلَفِ وَالْأَئِمَّةِ وَلَيْسَ فِيهِمْ مَنْ أَنْكَرَ بِسَبَبِ تَأَخُّرِهِ. وَإِذَا طَلَبَ الزِّيَادَةَ فَلَيْسَ لَهُ إلَّا الْأُجْرَةُ الْمُسَمَّاةُ وَإِنْ كَانَ غَرَّهُ فَذَاكَ شَيْءٌ آخَرُ لِيُبَيِّنْهُ السَّائِلُ حَتَّى يُجَابَ عَنْهُ.
translated_text:
He—may Allah have mercy on him—was asked:

A man holds a qīrāt share in some land and leases it to someone for 160 irdabbs—80 irdabbs less than others charge—before irrigation has reached it. Is the lease valid before irrigation reaches the land? May he demand its rental value?

He replied:

If these lands are ordinarily irrigated, leasing them before they have been irrigated is valid according to the jurists generally. The disagreement is confined to the school of al-Shāfi'ī, whose apparent position permits leasing such land, as do the other imams. The unqualified wording concerning the contract found in some of his books has been explained by the leading scholars of his school—may Allah be pleased with them.

Land in Egypt has always been leased before irrigation reached it, throughout the times of the early generations and the imams. None of them objected on account of the delay in irrigation.

If he demands an increase, he is entitled only to the stipulated rent. If, however, he was deceived, that is another matter, which the questioner should clarify so that it can be answered.

translated_text:
He was also asked:

A man leased out land forming part of his land grant for a specified term. The lessee took possession of the land, and the lessor received part of the rent. The lessee then recovered the rent he had paid to the lessor and terminated the lease. He subsequently stated that he had ploughed part of the land and demanded that the lessor pay for the ploughing. Is the lessor entitled to an amount equivalent to the cost of ploughing merely on the lessee’s statement, or not? May the lessor rescind the lease without a valid basis in Islamic law?

He replied:

If the lessee rescinded the lease after taking possession of the land, then, provided that they mutually agreed to cancel the lease or that he rescinded it on valid grounds, he must pay rent proportionate to the duration of his possession of the land, and he is entitled to the customary value of his ploughing.

He—may Allah have mercy on him—was asked:

Concerning the trustee of an endowment or an orphan’s property: may he hand over premises belonging to the endowment or the orphan’s property for someone to occupy without a lease valid under Islamic law? And if someone calls witnesses to attest to his declaration that he has leased specified premises from the endowment’s managing agent for a specified term

translated_text:
at a specified rent, paid the rent to the managing agent, took possession of the premises from them and occupied them for a time, and they then demanded the rent already paid, may the trustee make this lease binding on the tenant but not binding on himself and his deputies? May he invoke it to prevent the tenant from leaving when he wishes to leave and demand the rent specified in it, while accepting any higher offer from someone who outbids him? If this is impermissible and the trustee persists in it, does that compromise his integrity and his standing as trustee? Must he lease the endowment property or the orphan’s property under a valid lease, or not?

He replied:

He may not hand over endowment property, an orphan’s property, or any other property that he administers by virtue of his trusteeship except under a lease valid under Islamic law. He may not hand it over to the tenant under an invalid lease. Likewise, an agent acting for his principal may not hand over property he has been commissioned to lease except under a lease valid under Islamic law.

The trustee may not make the lease binding on the tenant but revocable by the lessor, for this contradicts the consensus of the Muslims. Rather, if he holds that leases, sales and similar transactions are valid when concluded through customary means—as the majority hold—he may hand over the property through an arrangement customarily recognized as a lease. If, however, he holds that sales, leases and similar transactions are valid only through a verbal formula, he must not hand over the property unless he has concluded the lease verbally. Likewise, he must not hand over anything he has sold from an orphan’s property or other property unless he has concluded a sale valid under Islamic law. Thus, whoever considers a sale concluded by mutual exchange without a verbal formula permissible may hand over the property on the basis of such a sale. This is the view

translated_text:
held by the majority of the imams and followed in Muslim practice from the time of their Prophet to the present day.

Whoever holds that a sale is not valid without a verbal formula from both parties may not, while holding that belief, hand over an orphan’s property except under a valid contract, such as a lease or a sale. In leases, sales and similar contracts—which the majority permit without a verbal formula, whereas some scholars permit them only with one—everyone must act consistently with the view he holds, whether it works to his advantage or against him. No one may adopt one view to determine his rights and the other to determine his obligations.

An example is someone who holds that, when he is a neighbor, he is entitled to a neighbor’s right of preemption, but when he is the purchaser, he need not honor that right. Another is someone who holds that, when he is one of the maternal half-siblings in the shared-inheritance case known as al-Himāriyya, the full siblings are excluded, but when he is one of the full siblings, he is entitled to share with the maternal half-siblings. Likewise, someone may hold that, when he is the plaintiff, judgment should be given in his favor on the basis of an oath referred back to him, and when he is the claimant, judgment should be given in his favor on the basis of one witness and an oath. There are many similar examples.

By agreement of the Muslims, no one may adopt such an approach to a disputed question. This amounts to permitting himself what he forbids someone in the same position, and forbidding that person what he permits himself; imposing obligations on another person in the same position that he does not impose on himself; and claiming rights for himself against others that he does not recognize for someone in the same position. It is necessarily known in the religion of Islam—indeed, in every religion—that this is impermissible. Whoever believes it permissible is a disbeliever. Indeed, whoever holds to the validity of

 الْمُسْتَأْجِرِينَ مِنْ الْخُرُوجِ. وَكَانَ بِمَنْزِلَةِ مَنْ سَلَّمَ الْعَيْنَ إلَى الْغَاصِبِ فَمَا تَلِفَ تَحْتَ يَدِ الْمُسْتَوْلِي كَانَ عَلَيْهِ ضَمَانُهُ كَمَا لَوْ سَلَّمَ مَالَهُ بِعَقْدِ فَاسِدٍ يَعْتَقِدُ هُوَ فَسَادَهُ وَإِنْ اعْتَقَدَ صِحَّةَ هَذَا الْعَقْدِ كَانَ لَهُ تَسْلِيمُ الْعَيْنِ وَالْمُطَالَبَةُ بِالْأُجْرَةِ الْمُسَمَّاةِ وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ أَنْ يَقْبَلَ زِيَادَةً عَلَى الْمُسْتَأْجِرِ وَلَا يُخْرِجَهُ قَبْلَ انْقِضَاءِ الْأُجْرَةِ مِنْ غَيْرِ سَبَبٍ شَرْعِيٍّ يُوجِبُ الْفَسْخَ. وَمَتَى أَصَرَّ النَّاظِرُ عَلَى أَنْ يَجْعَلَهُ فَاسِدًا بِالنِّسْبَةِ إلَى الْمُسْتَأْجِرِ صَحِيحًا بِالنِّسْبَةِ إلَيْهِ غَيْرَ لَازِمٍ بِالنِّسْبَةِ إلَى الْمُسْتَأْجِرِ؛ فَإِنَّهُ ظَالِمٌ جَائِرٌ وَذَلِكَ قَادِحٌ فِي وِلَايَتِهِ وَعَدَالَتِهِ. وَعَلَيْهِ أَنْ يُؤَجِّرَ مَا يُؤَجِّرُهُ إجَارَةً صَحِيحَةً وَلَيْسَ لَهُ بِاتِّفَاقِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ أَنْ يُؤَجِّرَ إجَارَةً يَعْلَمُ أَنَّهَا غَيْرُ صَحِيحَةٍ. وَاَللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ.

(١) ما بين معقوفتين غير موجود في المطبوع، ولم أقف عليه في كتاب صيانة مجموع الفتاوى من السقط والتصحيف
أسامة بن الزهراء - منسق الكتاب للموسوعة الشاملة
translated_text:
a sale concluded by exchange without a verbal formula, and similar leases that customary practice recognizes as sales and leases, holds that such a contract is valid whether concluded by himself or by others. Whoever considers it invalid considers it invalid whether concluded by himself or by others.

Thus, if the trustee acting as lessor holds either of these two views, he must abide by it, whether it works to his advantage or against him. If he considers this contract invalid, he may neither hand over the leased property, demand the stipulated rent, nor [prevent] (1) the tenants from leaving. He would be like someone who hands property over to a usurper: he would be liable for whatever perishes while in the possession of the person who has taken control, just as if he had handed over his own property under an invalid contract that he himself considers invalid.

If, however, he considers this contract valid, he may hand over the property and demand the stipulated rent. He may not accept a higher offer over that of the tenant, nor evict him before the lease expires without a ground recognized by Islamic law that warrants rescission.

Whenever the trustee insists on treating the contract as invalid with respect to the tenant, valid with respect to himself, and nonbinding with respect to the tenant, he is unjust and oppressive. This impugns his fitness to serve as trustee and his uprightness. He must lease whatever he lets under a valid lease. By agreement of the Muslims, he may not enter into a lease that he knows to be invalid. And Allah knows best.

وَسُئِلَ - رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ -:
عَنْ رَجُلٍ عَلَيْهِ حِصَّةُ وَقْفٍ وَعَلَيْهِ دَيْنٌ لِشَخْصِ فَأَجَّرَهُ الضَّيْعَةَ وَقَاصَّهُ بِدَيْنِهِ الْمَذْكُورِ عَلَيْهِ ثَلَاثَ سِنِينَ وَهُوَ شَرْطُ مَذْهَبِ الْوَاقِفِ وَعَلَيْهِ دَيْنٌ آخَرُ لِرَجُلِ آخَرَ فَاعْتَقَلَهُ فِي حَبْسِ السِّيَاسَةِ مُدَّةً إلَى أَنْ هَلَكَ مِنْ السِّجْنِ وَحَلَفَ أَنَّهُ مَا يُخْرِجُهُ حَتَّى يُضَمِّنَهُ الْحِصَّةَ فَمَا وَجَدَ مِنْ الْحَبْسِ وَالتَّهْدِيدِ ضَمَّنَّهُ الْحِصَّةَ الْمَذْكُورَةَ وَهُوَ ضَامِنُ حِصَّةٍ أُخْرَى فَاسْتَوْلَى عَلَيْهَا مِنْ أَوَّلِ الْمُدَّةِ وَمُدَّةُ الْإِيجَارِ خَمْسُ سِنِينَ وَمَبْلَغُ الدَّيْنِ وَاحِدٌ. فَهَلْ يَعْمَلُ بِالْإِيجَارَةِ الْأُولَى الَّتِي هِيَ شَرْطُ الْوَاقِفِ وَأَغْلَى قِيمَةً؟ أَمْ بِالثَّانِيَةِ الَّتِي هِيَ كُرْهٌ وَإِجْبَارٌ وَدُونَ الْقِيمَةِ وَغَيْرُ شَرْطِ الْوَاقِفِ؟ وَإِذَا كَانَ قَدْ أَخَذَ مِنْهَا مُغَلَّاتٍ يَرْجِعُ عَلَى الْمُسْتَأْجِرِ الْأَوَّلِ أَمْ لَا؟ وَإِذَا كَانَ قَدْ فَرَغَ مُدَّةَ الْأَوَّلِ لِمَنْ يَكُونُ وِلَايَةُ الْإِيجَارِ؟ .
فَأَجَابَ:
الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، إذَا كَانَ قَدْ أَجَّرَهُ إجَارَةً صَحِيحَةً كَانَتْ إجَارَتُهُ تِلْكَ الْمُدَّةَ أَوْ بَعْضَهَا قَبْلَ انْقِضَاءِ مُدَّةِ هَذِهِ الْإِجَارَةِ إجَارَةً بَاطِلَةً سَوَاءٌ كَانَتْ بِاخْتِيَارِ الْمُؤَجِّرِ أَوْ كَانَ قَدْ أُكْرِهَ عَلَيْهَا وَكَانَ هَذَا الْمُسْتَأْجِرُ ظَالِمًا بِوَضْعِ يَدِهِ عَلَيْهَا وَاسْتِغْلَالِهَا وَكَانَ لِلْمُسْتَأْجِرِ الْأَوَّلِ الْخِيَارُ بَيْنَ أَنْ يَفْسَخَ
translated_text:
He—may Allah have mercy on him—was asked:

About a man responsible for a share of an endowment who owed someone a debt. He leased the estate to that creditor for three years, offsetting the rent against the debt he owed him, this being the requirement of the legal school followed by the endowment’s founder. He owed another man a debt as well. This second creditor had him confined in the governing authorities’ prison for a time, until imprisonment had broken him, and swore that he would not release him until he leased him the share. Because of the imprisonment and threats he suffered, he leased him the aforementioned share. The creditor was already leasing another share, and took possession from the beginning of the term. This lease was for five years, while the amount of the debt was the same.

Should effect be given to the first lease, which accords with the founder’s stipulation and provides a higher rent, or to the second, which was obtained through coercion and compulsion, is below the proper rental value, and contravenes the founder’s stipulation? If he has already collected revenue from it, is there recourse against the first tenant or not? Once the first tenant’s term has expired, who has the authority to lease it?

He replied:

Praise be to Allah. If he had leased it under a valid lease, then any further lease he granted for that same period, or part of it, before the existing lease expired would be invalid, whether the lessor entered into it voluntarily or was coerced. This latter tenant would be acting wrongfully by taking possession of the property and drawing revenue from it. The first tenant would have the choice between rescinding

الْإِجَارَةَ وَتَسْقُطَ عَنْهُ الْأُجْرَةُ مِنْ حِينِ الْفَسْخِ وَبَيْنَ أَنْ يَضْمَنَهَا فَيُؤَدِّي الْأُجْرَةَ وَيُطَالِبُ هَذَا الظَّالِمَ بِعِوَضِ الْمَنْفَعَةِ.
وَسُئِلَ:
عَنْ دَارٍ وُقِفَ عَلَى صَغِيرٍ وَرَجُلٍ بَالِغٍ وَقَدْ أَجَّرَهَا أَبُو الْوَاقِفِ بِالْإِكْرَاهِ وَالْإِجْبَارِ مِنْ رَجُلٍ لَهُ جَاهٌ مُنْذُ أَرْبَعِينَ سَنَةً. فَهَلْ تَصِحُّ إجَارَةُ الْأَبِ عَلَى ابْنِهِ الْبَالِغِ؟ وَقَدْ رَآهُ مُكْرَهًا وَعَلَيْهِ التَّرْسِيمُ فَأَرَادَ الِابْنُ خَلَاصَهُ مِنْ يَدِ الظَّالِمِ الَّذِي أَكْرَهَ عَلَى الْإِيجَارِ فَأَشْهَدَ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ بِإِمْضَاءِ الْإِجَارَةِ فَهَلْ يَصِحُّ هَذَا الْإِشْهَادُ؟ وَهَلْ تَصِحُّ إجَارَةُ أَرْبَعِينَ سَنَةً؟ .
فَأَجَابَ:
إذَا أُكْرِهَ عَلَى الْإِيجَارِ بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ أَوْ أُكْرِهَ بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ عَلَى تَنْفِيذِهَا:
 لَمْ يَصِحَّ؛ فَإِنَّ الْمُكْرَهَ بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ لَا يُلْزَمُ بَيْعَهُ وَلَا إجَارَتَهُ وَلَا إنْفَاذَهُ بِاتِّفَاقِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ. وَأَمَّا إجَارَةُ الْوَقْفِ هَذِهِ الْمُدَّةَ فَفِيهَا نِزَاعٌ بَيْنَ الْعُلَمَاءِ كَمَا فِي مَذْهَبِ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ وَالشَّافِعِيِّ.
translated_text:
the lease, with his liability for rent ceasing from the time of rescission, and remaining liable under it, paying the rent, and demanding compensation from this wrongdoer for the use of the property.

He was asked:

About a house endowed for the benefit of a minor and an adult man. The founder’s father leased it forty years ago under coercion and compulsion from an influential man. Is the father’s lease valid with respect to his adult son? The son saw that his father was being coerced and held under guard. Wishing to free him from the wrongdoer who had forced him to grant the lease, the son formally declared before witnesses that he ratified it. Is this witnessed declaration valid? And is a forty-year lease valid?

He replied:

If someone is wrongfully coerced into granting a lease or wrongfully coerced into ratifying it, it is not valid. By the consensus of the Muslims, someone subjected to wrongful coercion is not bound by his sale, lease, or ratification. As for leasing an endowment for this length of time, scholars disagree, as is the case within the schools of Abū Hanīfah and al-Shāfiʿī.

وَسُئِلَ - رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ -:
عَنْ أَيْتَامٍ لَهُمْ نَصِيبٌ فِي مِلْكٍ فَأَجَّرَهُ الْوَصِيُّ لِلشَّرِكَةِ مُدَّةَ ثَلَاثِ سِنِينَ بِدُونِ قِيمَةِ الْمِثْلِ. فَمَا الْحُكْمُ؟ .
فَأَجَابَ:
الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، مَتَى أَجَّرَهُ الْوَصِيُّ بِدُونِ أُجْرَةِ الْمِثْلِ كَانَ ضَامِنًا لِمَا فَوَّتَهُ عَلَى الْيَتِيمِ وَلَمْ تَكُنْ الْإِجَارَةُ لَازِمَةً لِلْيَتِيمِ بَعْدَ رُشْدِهِ؛ بَلْ هِيَ بَاطِلَةٌ مُنْفَسِخَةٌ فِي أَحَدِ قَوْلَيْ الْعُلَمَاءِ. وَفِي الْآخَرِ لَهُ أَنْ يَفْسَخَهَا. ثُمَّ إنْ كَانَ الْمُسْتَأْجِرُ لَمْ يَعْلَمْ تَحْرِيمَ مَا فَعَلَهُ الْوَصِيُّ كَانَ لَهُ أَنْ يَضْمَنَهُ مَا لَمْ يَلْتَزِمْ ضَمَانَهُ وَإِنْ عَلِمَ اسْتَقَرَّ الضَّمَانُ عَلَيْهِ؛ بَلْ لَوْ أَجَّرَهُ بِأُجْرَةِ الْمِثْلِ. مِثْلَ هَذِهِ الْمُدَّةِ الَّتِي يَعْلَمُ الْوَصِيُّ أَنَّهُ يَبْلُغُ فِي أَثْنَائِهَا؛ فَأَكْثَرُ الْعُلَمَاءِ يُجَوِّزُونَ لِلْيَتِيمِ الْفَسْخَ. وَاَللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ.
translated_text:
He—may Allah have mercy on him—was asked:

About orphans who own a share in a property, which their guardian leased to the partnership for three years at less than the fair rental value. What is the ruling?

He replied:

Praise be to Allah. If the guardian leases it for less than the fair rental value, he is liable for the loss he has caused the orphan. The lease is not binding on the orphan after he attains sound judgment. Rather, according to one of the two scholarly opinions, it is invalid and automatically dissolved; according to the other, the orphan may rescind it.

If the lessee did not know that the guardian’s action was unlawful, he may hold the guardian liable for any liability he had not undertaken himself. If he knew, however, ultimate liability rests with him. Indeed, even if the guardian leased it at the fair rental value for a term during which he knows the orphan will come of age, most scholars allow the orphan to rescind the lease. And Allah knows best.

إذَا كَانَتْ الضَّرِيبَةُ وَمُؤَجِّرُهَا يُؤَجِّرُهَا بِهَا سَوَاءٌ كَانَ الْفَلَّاحُ يَقْتَرِضُ أَوْ لَمْ يَكُنْ. وَلَمْ يُرِدْ الضَّرِيبَةَ لِأَجْلِ الْقُوَّةِ فَهَذَا جَائِزٌ؛ فَإِنَّ الْقَرْضَ لَمْ يَجُرَّ بِهِ مَنْفَعَةً وَإِنْ كَانَ بَعْضُ الْعُلَمَاءِ كَرِهَ ذَلِكَ وَجَعَلَهُ مِنْ الْقَرْضِ الَّذِي يَجُرُّ مَنْفَعَةً؛ إذْ بِالْقُوَّةِ يَسْتَأْجِرُهَا الْفَلَّاحُ لَكِنَّ هَذِهِ مَنْفَعَةٌ
translated_text:
He was asked:

About a man who rented a house, after which a bathhouse was built beside it. Its water breeds mosquitoes, and his wife miscarried because of the smell of its smoke. May he rescind the lease?

He replied:

If the tenant did not know that operating this bathhouse would cause harm that ordinarily diminishes the value of the property’s use, he may rescind the lease. His statement that he did not know is accepted if supported by his oath. And Allah knows best.

He was asked:

About a land grant leased under a registered agreement at three ardabbs and three dirhams per feddan, with cultivation advances to be supplied by the grantee and the oxen supplied by the tenants. Is this permissible or not?

He replied:

If the lessor leases it at the stipulated rental charge whether or not the farmer borrows, and does not seek that charge on account of the advance, this is permissible, since the loan has brought him no benefit. Some scholars, however, have disliked this and considered it a loan that brings a benefit, since the advance enables the farmer to lease the land. But this is a benefit

translated_text:
to both parties. If he does not increase the rent on account of the advance, he has done well. It makes no difference whether it is called a lease or a registered agreement; both are the same.

He was asked:

About a man who hired a worker to tend an orchard, but the worker stopped working until part of the orchard was ruined. Is he entitled to his wages? Is he liable for compensation or not?

He replied:

There is no doubt that if he fails to perform the work stipulated in his agreement, he is not entitled to his wages. If he performs part of it, he is paid in proportion to the work he has done. If any property is lost or damaged through his negligence, he is liable for that loss or damage. Negligence means failing, without an excuse, to perform what one is obliged to do.

He was asked:

Regarding a riding animal: Which is better—to carry people free of charge, or to charge a fare and give it in charity?

He replied:

If they are poor, it is better to waive their fare. If they are wealthy and there is someone in need, it is better to collect the fare for the benefit of that person.

 فَهَلْ لِرَبِّ الْأَرْضِ قَلْعُهُ بِمَا أَنْفَقُوهُ؟ عَلَى قَوْلَيْنِ مَشْهُورَيْنِ لِلْعُلَمَاءِ.

 فَلَهُ ذَلِكَ بِالِاتِّفَاقِ.
translated_text:
He—may Allah have mercy on him—was asked:

About someone who leased land belonging to the public treasury to certain individuals, each lease specifying a particular area at a specified rent in dirhams. Plantings were established on the land, but the land held by the tenants included an additional area beyond that recorded in their leases. Is it permissible to survey the land and recover the excess for the public treasury?

He replied:

Whatever they have planted beyond the area to which their leases entitle them is subject to the customary rent. Whenever they use the excess land, they must pay the customary rent, by agreement of the Muslims.

If they have not used it, may the landowner uproot the plantings upon reimbursing what they have spent? The scholars hold two well-known opinions on this.

If he chooses to leave the plantings in place and demand the customary rent, he is entitled to do so by agreement.

فَأَجَابَ:
إنْ كَانَتْ صَحِيحَةً فَهِيَ لَازِمَةٌ مِنْ الطَّرَفَيْنِ بِاتِّفَاقِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَلَيْسَ لِلْمُؤَجِّرِ أَنْ يُخْرِجَ الْمُسْتَأْجِرَ؛ لِأَجْلِ زِيَادَةٍ حَصَلَتْ عَلَيْهِ وَالْحَالُ هَذِهِ. وَلَا يَقْبَلُ عَلَيْهِ زِيَادَةً وَالْحَالُ هَذِهِ بِاتِّفَاقِ الْأَئِمَّةِ. وَإِنْ كَانَتْ الْإِجَارَةُ فَاسِدَةً لَمْ يَجُزْ لِنَاظِرِ الْوَقْفِ أَنْ يُمَكِّنَ الْمُسْتَأْجِرَ مِنْ تَسَلُّمِ الْمَكَانِ بِمِثْلِ هَذِهِ الْإِجَارَةِ وَلَا لَهُ أَنْ يَمْنَعَهُ مِنْ الْخُرُوجِ إذَا أَرَادَ وَلَا يَمْلِكُ أَنْ يُطَالِبَهُ بِالْأُجْرَةِ الْمُسَمَّاةِ فِي الْعَقْدِ وَكَانَ دُخُولُ النَّاظِرِ فِي مِثْلِ ذَلِكَ قَادِحًا فِي عَدَالَتِهِ وَوِلَايَتِهِ؛ فَإِنَّهُ يَجِبُ عَلَيْهِ بِاتِّفَاقِ الْأَئِمَّةِ أَنْ لَا يُؤَجِّرَ الْمَكَانَ إلَّا إجَارَةً صَحِيحَةً فِي الشَّرْعِ وَيَجِبُ عَلَيْهِ بِاتِّفَاقِ الْأَئِمَّةِ إذَا أَجَّرَهُ كَذَلِكَ أَنْ لَا يَقْبَلَ الزِّيَادَةَ عَلَى الْمُسْتَأْجِرِ وَلَا يُخْرِجَهُ لِأَجْلِهَا. وَأَمَّا الَّذِي زَادَ عَلَى الْمُسْتَأْجِرِ. فَلَوْ زَادَ عَلَيْهِ بَعْدَ رُكُونِ الْمُؤَجِّرِ
translated_text:
He—may Allah have mercy on him—was asked:

About someone who rented premises from their administrators for a specified term at a specified rent. If he wished to be released from the lease, they would not release him before its term expired. May they accept a higher offer from someone else before his lease expires?

He replied:

If the lease is valid, it is binding on both parties by agreement of the Muslims. In these circumstances, the landlord may not evict the tenant because someone has offered a higher rent. Nor may he accept a higher offer over the tenant’s, by agreement of the imams.

If the lease is invalid, the endowment’s trustee may not allow the tenant to take possession of the premises under such a lease. Nor may he prevent him from leaving if he wishes, or demand the rent specified in the contract. The trustee’s entering into such an arrangement would call into question both his integrity and his trusteeship. By agreement of the imams, he must lease the premises only under a contract valid according to Islamic law. Likewise, by agreement of the imams, once he has leased them under such a contract, he must not accept a higher offer over the tenant’s or evict him on that account.

As for the person who offered more than the tenant, if he made a higher offer after the landlord had become favourably disposed

 فَأَجَّرَهُ بِدُونِ أُجْرَةِ الْمِثْلِ كَانَ ظَالِمًا ضَامِنًا لِمَا نَقَصَ أَهْلَ الْوَقْفِ مِنْ أُجْرَةِ الْمِثْلِ. وَلَوْ تَغَيَّرَتْ أَسْعَارُ الْعَقَارِ بَعْدَ الْإِجَارَةِ الشَّرْعِيَّةِ لَمْ يَمْلِكْ الْفَسْخَ بِذَلِكَ فَإِنَّ هَذَا لَا يَنْضَبِطُ وَلَا يَدْخُلُ فِي التَّكْلِيفِ. وَالْمَنْفَعَةُ بِالنِّسْبَةِ إلَى الزَّمَانِ قَدْ تَكُونُ مُخْتَلِفَةً لَا مُمَاثِلَةً. فَتَكُونُ قِيمَتُهَا فِي الشِّتَاءِ
translated_text:
to leasing it to him, he would have bid over his brother’s bid. If he offered more after the contract had been concluded, while rescission was still possible, he would be like someone who undercuts his brother’s sale. Both are forbidden by the explicit words of the Messenger of Allah—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—and this is the position of the four imams. How much more serious, then, is offering more when a valid lease is already in force! Such a bidder is disobedient, sinful and unjust, and deserves discretionary punishment. Whoever helps him in this has helped him in sin and transgression.

The tenant’s having his own commitment witnessed, without the landlord doing likewise, makes no difference here, for the contract does not require witnesses; it is valid without them. The trustee’s saying to him, “Have your commitment witnessed,” together with the tenant’s doing so, constitutes a lease valid according to Islamic law. Indeed, once the trustee has told him, “Have your commitment witnessed,” no one may offer more than he has.

The trustee must not lease the premises until he considers it most likely that no one will offer more. He must publicize their availability among prospective tenants who customarily rent such premises. Once he has done so, he has leased them at the going rate, and this is a lease valid according to Islamic law.

If, however, he favours one of his friends, someone who has done him a favour, or anyone else by leasing the premises below the going rate, he is acting unjustly and is liable for the shortfall in the rent due to the endowment’s beneficiaries.

If property rental rates change after a valid lease has been concluded, he has no right to rescind it on that account, for such fluctuations cannot be precisely controlled and fall outside what one can be required to account for. The value of the benefit derived from the property may vary over time rather than remain uniform. Thus, its value in winter

translated_text:
may exceed its value in summer, or vice versa. Someone who rents it for a year accepts paying more during certain parts of the rental period in view of its higher value at other times. No one may therefore outbid him because the rental value of those premises has risen. If the lease were to terminate during part of that period, the amount would be apportioned according to the respective rental values, not merely the lengths of time involved.

Thus, one asks: “What is its rental value during the summer?” The rent is then apportioned according to its value at each time, with each period assigned a share of the rent proportionate to its rental value.

The trustee must act in the endowment’s best interests when leasing the premises, whether yearly, monthly or daily. If its interests are best served by leasing them day by day, so that at the end of each day the tenant may vacate and the landlord may require him to do so, he should adopt that arrangement. If its interests are best served by a monthly lease, so that at the beginning of each month the tenant may vacate and the landlord may require him to do so, he should adopt that arrangement. But if a yearly lease serves its interests, he has fulfilled his duty and may not evict the tenant before the lease expires merely to obtain a higher rent.

As for the distinction drawn by some later jurists among the followers of al-Shāfiʿī and Imam Ahmad between an increase amounting to one-third and one amounting to less, this is an innovated opinion with no basis in the teachings of any of the imams—neither al-Shāfiʿī nor Ahmad nor anyone else—whether concerning endowments or other property.

He—may Allah have mercy on him—was also asked:

A man rented a shop from the administrators of endowments for a specified term at a specified rent. He took possession of the shop and used it, and they collected the rent due to them. Had he sought release from the lease, they would not have released him until the term expired. May they accept a higher offer from someone else before his lease expires, or not?

He replied:

They may not accept a higher offer in these circumstances, whether the property is an endowment, belongs to an orphan, or is otherwise owned.

Anyone who considers it permissible to accept a higher offer while refusing to allow the tenant to withdraw when he wishes has contravened the consensus of the Muslims. If the lease is invalid or impermissible, both the landlord and the tenant may withdraw from it. If it is valid and binding, neither may terminate it merely for a higher rent or the like, without grounds warranting termination. To treat it as revocable on the landlord’s side but binding on the tenant’s side is contrary to the consensus of the Muslims.

Moreover, if the trustee claims that he did not lease these premises, or that he leased them under an invalid contract, this would call his administration and integrity into question, for it amounts to an admission on his part that he is handing over

Moreover, this amounts to an admission that the tenant is not liable for the stipulated rent, but only for the fair rental value. The fair rental value is often less than the stipulated rent, so this constitutes an admission that he is liable for the loss he has caused the endowment’s beneficiaries. If the trustee claimed that the lease was invalid while the tenant maintained that it was valid, the statement of the party asserting its validity would prevail, since contracts between Muslims are presumed valid. And Allah knows best.

He—may Allah be pleased with him—was also asked:

A man works as a weigher using a qabbān (weighing balance), and takes his fee from those for whom he weighs goods. Is this permissible for him? Is the fee lawful or unlawful?

He replied:

Praise be to Allah. Weighing with an accurate qabbān balance is like weighing with any other scales. If the weigher uses these accurate instruments fairly, his weighing is permissible. If the instrument is faulty and the weigher gives short weight, he is among the wrongdoers and transgressors.

If he weighs fairly and takes his fee from the person responsible for having the goods weighed, that is permissible.

 " فَكَيْفَ حَرَّمَ هَذَا وَوَصَفَ بِالتَّدَاوِي هُنَا وَجَعَلَهُ شِفَاءً
original_footnote:
(١) ما بين معقوفتين غير موجود في المطبوع، ولم أقف عليه في كتاب صيانة مجموع الفتاوى من السقط والتصحيف
أسامة بن الزهراء - منسق الكتاب للموسوعة الشاملة
translated_text:
He was also asked:

A man stamps cloth, and another man lodges with him. If the man claims that the rent comes from a source other than his earnings, is it permissible to accept it?

He replied:

If he has another lawful source of income, states that he is paying the rent from it, and is thought likely to be telling the truth, [it is permissible] (1) to accept it. If he is not thought likely to be lying, he may be believed in this matter, provided he is not known to be lying.

He—may Allah have mercy on him—was also asked:

Is a cupper’s fee unlawful? Does food he prepares with his hands become ritually impure? Did the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, pay the cupper his fee? What reports prohibit it?

Has it been reported in a hadith that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Healing for my community lies in three things: a verse from the Book of Allah, a lick of honey, or a cupping treatment administered by a cupper”?

How, then, did he prohibit this, yet prescribe it here as a treatment and describe it as a cure?
